finding.claim: _validate_sub returns early when the token has no 'sub' claim, so a caller-supplied subject= check is skipped. A validly signed token without 'sub' passes a subject-bound check. iss and aud do not have this gap (missing claim raises MissingRequiredClaimError).
finding.source: Token issued by the same issuer that lacks a 'sub' claim (e.g. verification, reset or service token). Attacker needs one such token.
finding.sink: Subject-bound authorization check in the application: jwt.decode(token, key, algorithms=[...], subject=...)

trace.note: _validate_sub returns early when 'sub' not in payload
subject comparison is never reached for subject-less tokens

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified first (api_jws.py:277-285); alg allow-list enforced; iss/aud raise on missing claim (api_jwt.py:571-572, 529-532). Only sub is skipped. Likely upstream PyJWT behaviour, possibly intentional.

finding.claim: With cache_keys=True, the per-kid signing-key cache (lru_cache on get_signing_key) has no time-based expiry. A PyJWK removed from the JWKS after rotation or compromise keeps validating tokens until LRU eviction, which only happens when more than max_cached_keys other kids are used.
finding.source: Holder of a former signing key (compromised or rotated out) who forges tokens with that kid.
finding.sink: Token signature verification accepting a revoked key: PyJWKClient.get_signing_key_from_jwt(token) returns the cached key, then decode() verifies with it.

trace.note: get_signing_key returns cached PyJWK for a kid that already resolved
docstring documents no time-based expiration for tier 2

finding.guards_checked: Tier-1 JWKSetCache does expire (jwk_set_cache.py:25-31), so the removed key drops out of the JWKS after lifespan; only the tier-2 cache retains it. Behaviour is documented, not hidden.

finding.claim: A token whose kid matches no key forces an unconditional synchronous JWKS refetch (get_signing_keys(refresh=True)). Failed lookups are not cached, so every unauthenticated token with a bogus kid causes one outbound request to the IdP JWKS endpoint.
finding.source: Any unauthenticated client sending a JWT with an arbitrary 'kid' header to an endpoint that calls get_signing_key_from_jwt.
finding.sink: Outbound HTTP request in fetch_data (jwks_client.py:135) with no negative cache or cooldown.

trace.note: get_signing_key_from_jwt reads kid from unverified header
get_signing_keys() uses cache first, no match
get_jwk_set bypasses cache when refresh is True

finding.guards_checked: JWKS URI fixed by developer and restricted to http/https (jwks_client.py:90-95); redirects blocked (jwks_client.py:17-27); jku/x5u never used; kid only used for lookup in a trusted set. Attacker cannot choose the destination, only the frequency.
